x: We were well placed at the start, and after about a mile and a half Hines, of Surrey, was leading, followed by Belton (Surrey), Thorogood (Mitcham), with about nine of ours in the first thirty.

When the runners were next seen, at about half distance, Carter was in the first three, together with Brown (Mitcham) and Hines (Surrey), with Penny (7th), Kemp (25th), Lucas (27th), Herbert (28th) and Mick Walker (30th) completing our scoring six.
Hines ran well to win the 2 Miles race for the South. The North won the 1 Mile Medley Relay and also the Team race held in connection with the 5 Miles Road Walk.

Allen (N.F.S.), the old Highgate International had the measure of the field in the mile which was perhaps the best race of the afternoon, with Hines 2nd, Forde 3rd and Freddy White 4th, in the excellent time of 4.36.

… Hoath, who revels in hard work: he won the " C.D." Mile, Open Mile and was 4th in the 2 miles Team Race. Our old rival Hines, of Surrey A.C., Stockport, Epsom, Banstead, C.T.C., etc., etc., etc., ran away with the 2 miles in 9.44.…

We were well placed at the start, and after about a mile and a half Hines, of Surrey, was leading, with about nine of ours in the first thirty.At three miles Bert Footer was on Hines' shoulder, having apparently done a bit of "snaky" running when out of the sight of spectators.

Performances from Hines, Carlos, Evans and company confirmed the former and our fears over the altitude question were supported not only by abysmal British performances but also by below par efforts by 'greats' such as Ryun, Roelants and Haase.
